_comment: Customer-facing copy for the 'What the configuration includes' section.
This section is NOT a second copy of the Configuration table. The table says
what is in the crate; this says what the customer gets out of the machine.
A module is written here only if BOTH are true:
1. its class is in 'include_classes' below, and
2. someone has written copy for it in 'capabilities'.
Entries marked group 'furthermore' skip the class test - they are offer
extras the sales manager chose to call out, not machine features.
Copy can exist for a module that the class filter keeps out. That is fine and
deliberate: widening 'include_classes' later then costs nothing.
'class_overrides' reclassifies a module everywhere - the Configuration table's
class rows as well as this section - so a module filed oddly by the
configurator lands where it belongs in both places.
Entry fields:
text     - the line the customer reads. Lead with what they get.
bullets  - optional sub-points, indented one level under the line.
group    - 'main' (default) or 'furthermore'.
aliases  - other codes that reuse this copy.
DRAFT WARNING: everything except DUALPROBESCOPE and NETDONGLE was drafted from
the configurator's own export descriptions and has not been reviewed by Sales.
Read a line before it goes to a customer. No figure here should be invented -
if a number is not in the export description or a previous offer, leave it out.
lead_in: The solution offered is N°1 unit {machine}, equipped with:

VX.text: Dual-side vertical flying probe with 8 flying electrical probes (4 + 4), giving full in-circuit and functional test capability on double-sided boards without a dedicated fixture.

8Z-HEADS-HR.text: 1 µm resolution Z motors on all 8 heads, for repeatable probing force and reliable contact on fine-pitch pads.

ACL.text: Measurement and stimuli motherboard with MONIACL - the analogue core that performs the in-circuit measurements.

ALI.text: 2 Laser sensors for warpage compensation and optical inspection (ALI) - the real board surface is mapped before probing, so contact stays accurate on bowed panels.

DUALPROBESCOPE.text: 2 High frequency mobile scope probes to measure up to 500 MHz (DUALPROBESCOPE), including picoscope macros that contain basic parameters designed to conduct:
bullets: All picoscope macros will include trigger options.
All macros will have the expected values and tolerance allowed by the user.

OBPFPDVC.text: 1 Seica general purpose programmer option for On-board programming (OBPFPDVC) - devices are programmed in place, with no separate programming step.

PRBOOST.text: PRBOOST feature which allows the user to get 2A from each of the 8 regular probes, so power rails and loads can be driven during functional test.

FLYSTRAIN.text: FLYSTRAIN option to measure the probes pressure applied to the UUT, keeping probing force inside the board's mechanical limits.

PRBVIEW.text: 4 CCD cameras PRBVIEW - the probes are seen directly during debug, so contact problems are visible rather than inferred.

MOTCAMS.text: Front and rear motorized CCD cameras (MOTCAMS) - focus adjusts for thick boards and tall components instead of being set by hand.

RFMEAS.text: RF measurement capability up to 100 MHz through the coax path on the standard probes, with no additional fixturing.

V8OFX.text: OPENFIX - Dual Side - 0 Angle Open Pin Detector Probe, for finding open pins that electrical test alone does not see.

FLYJTAG1.text: 1 Boundary Scan test with the integrated option - JTAG chains are exercised from the same program as the electrical test.

ICT.text: In circuit test software for shorts, opens, passives and semiconductors.

QT.text: Quick Test graphical operating system for functional test - sequences are built graphically rather than coded.

VIW.text: VIW - AOI capabilities + barcode reading, including 2D codes, so optical inspection and traceability happen in the same pass as electrical test.

FLYLAB.text: FLYLAB (manual tool for quick measurements) - interactive probing during debug without rerunning a program.

ERPS.text: ERPS - Enhanced Repair Station for diagnostic of reports, so the repair operator sees what failed and where.

VIVA.text: VIVA Test Operating System licence - the single environment in which programs are written, run and debugged.

STAT.text: Statistics software including XML and PPVS reporting and SPC tools (Cp, Cpk, GR&R) for monitoring process capability over time.

VLFUN.text: VIVA Language for functional test, for custom test steps where the standard library does not cover a device.

CAD.text: CAD software database used to generate test programs directly from board data.

MENTORPACK.text: CAD translators package based on Siemens Valor Process Preparation, including first year maintenance - board data from the major CAD systems is imported without manual conversion.

PSTDI.text: 1 programming station off-line (PSTDI) - programs are written and debugged away from the tester, so the machine keeps testing.

S64NTX.text: S64 matrix card with embedded traceability and extended performances, expanding the channels available to functional test.

S64H.text: 64 analogue channels matrix, high power, 500 VDC at 2 A.

SE5.text: Power supply controller, required for the PRBOOST option.

AP5.text: Programmable linear power supplies for powering the board under test.

LUV8M.text: Multi Magaziner loader and unloader, up to 5+1+5 racks with boards held vertically, for unattended in-line operation.

PASSFAIL.text: Good/bad board separation into the same magazine with an empty slot between them, so sorting needs no operator.

CLEA60.text: Z clearance extended from 40 mm to 60 mm, for taller assemblies.

AWAM.text: Automated width adjust for the board conveyor.

OPENFUN.text: Third party software caller from VIVA, for integrating test executables you already own.

RAIL8MM.text: Maximum UUT thickness extended from 5 mm to 8 mm.

FBBT4.text: Universal frame for irregularly shaped boards, suitable for manual and automated systems.

NETDONGLE.text: NETDONGLE: the existing NETDONGLE (SEICA P/N AE-D0NGLUSB-13) can be used to enable VIVA software on additional networked workstations, up to a maximum of ten (10) users.

DONGLERPS.text: Licence dongle for the Repair Station software, so the repair bench runs independently of the tester.

KEL.text: Large English keyboard supplied with the offline station.

M22-16/9.text: 23" 16:9 monitor supplied with the offline station.

PCW11TOW.text: PC tower, 64-bit, i7 9th generation, 16 GB RAM, 250 GB SSD and 1 TB hard disk, suitable for Windows 11.

PRTERFP.text: USB thermal ticket printer, 40 columns, for printing results at the machine.

UPS.text: 700 VA uninterruptible power supply, so a mains dip does not interrupt a test run or corrupt the system.

W11LTSC.text: Microsoft Windows 11 LTSC 64-bit licence - the long-term-servicing build, so feature updates cannot disturb a qualified test system.

230V_AUTO.text: The automation module runs from 230 Vac single phase instead of 400 Vac three phase, so no three-phase supply is needed at the installation site.

EMECOVE.text: Emergency circuitry separated from cover management, so the safety chain stays independent of the cover interlocks.

BXAUT.text: Wooden box for the automation module.

PACKVAC.text: Vacuum bag packaging, protecting the machine against moisture in transit.

PS 150V 5A.text: Customer-requested 150 V / 5 A power supply for the board under test.

One Doungle.text: One dongle for the offline programming and repair station.

two PCW11TOW.text: A second identical PC - one runs the system, the other serves as the programming and backup station.

MAGAZINE.text: 3 vertical magazines for the automation module.

M22-16/9TS.text: 23" 16:9 touch screen monitor on the machine itself.
